A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeoVerse and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched reliably despite expanded appendices and renumbered references.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and video-generation experiments, ablations, and qualitative application results, including Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds quantitative video-editing and 3D-tracking evaluations in Tables S2–S3.

M1.justification: The reconstruction architecture, bidirectional motion modeling, degradation simulation, training objectives, and inference procedures are unchanged. The new downstream evaluations use applications already described in v1.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation on FiVE for video editing and the DriveTrack subset of TAPVid-3D for 3D tracking. This substantially extends benchmark coverage for applications previously demonstrated only qualitatively. Existing training datasets and reconstruction/generation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Two new comparative evaluations introduce AnyV2V, Wan-Edit, and VACE for editing, and SpatialTracker and St4RTrack for tracking. These establish substantial downstream comparator coverage absent from v1; VACE's earlier citation did not constitute an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The added evaluations specify structural distance, CLIP score, NIQE, and seconds per frame for editing, and APD at a 0.1 m threshold and EPE for tracking. These are additional evaluation specifications; retained reconstruction splits, VBench settings, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: The ablations in Table 4, degradation and motion-tracking analyses, and illustrated failure cases are retained. Tables S2–S3 are additional task benchmarks, while the new linear-motion discussion supplies explanation without a new sensitivity or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables use point estimates, and the existing averaging practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables S2–S3 add substantial downstream results: editing takes 0.49 seconds/frame versus 3.07–6.11 for comparators, with mixed quality rankings; tracking APD/EPE is 7.31/3.10 versus SpatialTracker's 3.79/3.35 and St4RTrack's 2.47/5.64. Table 3 also revises TrajectoryCrafter's reconstruction time from 38 to 25 seconds and total time from 159 to 146 seconds, without a stated protocol change.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), mathematical definitions, and the approximate linear-motion assumption are unchanged. Appendix F discusses that existing assumption without adding a derivation, proof, or revised formal condition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable monocular training, versatility, and state-of-the-art reconstruction and generation. The downstream benchmarks provide new support without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix F argues that interpolation inaccuracies act as temporal degradation that generation can overcome, and identifies all-frame inference as a mitigation. Appendix E interprets the new results as competitive editing and reliable 3D correspondence. Existing text-rendering and 2D-cartoon limitations remain.

D1.justification: Table S3 newly identifies SpatialTracker predictions as supplied by TAPVid-3D and St4RTrack predictions as obtained from its official codebase. Table S1 improves dataset provenance with CoP3D and corrected HyperSim citations and removes HyperSim's 'Real' marker; this documents a correction rather than changed training data.

R1.justification: Seven references are added for St4RTrack, TAPVid-3D, AnyV2V, FiVE, SpatialTracker, HyperSim, and CoP3D. These support the added evaluations and improve dataset attribution; the related-work discussion and central research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts downstream-evaluation and linear-motion-discussion sections into the supplement, renumbers subsequent sections, and adds acknowledgements. Other changes are limited heading capitalization and bibliographic wording corrections, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Two compact tables, S2–S3, are added. Existing supplementary figures are redistributed across columns and pages, and references reflow. Figure contents and the principal main-text displays are retained, so the presentation change is limited.

improvement.justification: Tables S2–S3 add quantitative baseline comparisons where v1 offered only qualitative editing and tracking demonstrations, making the versatility claim better supported. Dataset attribution also improves. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new evaluation protocols and the absence of a dedicated test supporting the new linear-motion reassurance; the core scientific study remains stable.
